title: A five-shift fit reduced 2024-2025 buoy-change error where a variance match raised it at 30 OISST moorings
abstract: We tested whether local corrections of NOAA OISST v2.1 improve measured buoy temperature changes in later years. We fitted each station in 2022-2023 and scored 2024-2025 at 30 moorings. A variance match raised median mean squared error by 40.7 percent for one-day changes and 9.9 percent for seven-day changes. A five-shift ridge fit reduced error by 9.1 percent and 10.8 percent. The error ratios were 0.909 (conditional 95 percent spatial-group interval 0.820-0.933) and 0.892 (0.855-0.946). The fit also beat scalar regression. At 24 common stations, fits from 2016-2017 had 3.3 percent and 6.3 percent more error than recent fits on the same 2024-2025 targets. Both test years showed the main median directions. Removing the gross-pair filter kept the results. Stronger regularization made the seven-day benefit uncertain. This is a new held-out test on an existing daily archive, not independent observations or a new estimator. Buoys feed OISST, the sample has only four tropical stations, and two test years cannot establish global or long-term skill. The fit uses future OISST and a separate filter for each change interval. It does not produce a common corrected SST record or test heatwave trends. Code, aggregate errors, fit parameters, source hashes and reproduction steps are included. Daily source records stay outside this package.

display.caption: Corrections fitted in 2022-2023 and scored in 2024-2025. Bars show conditional 95 percent spatial-group intervals. Ratios below one mean less error.
